pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis THE SMOKING GUN: Pelvic transvaginal ultrasound revealing a small, occult mature ovarian teratoma alongside positive CSF IgG antibodies against the GluN1 (NR1) subunit. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Ectopic neural elements within an ovarian teratoma express NMDA receptors, triggering a systemic autoimmune response. Circulating IgG autoantibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and bind to the GluN1 subunit of NMDA receptors, causing receptor cross-linking, capping, and internalization. The resulting profound loss of NMDA receptor density on GABAergic inhibitory interneurons leads to disinhibition of cortical circuits. This manifests sequentially as psychiatric symptoms, involuntary orofacial movements, drug-resistant seizures, autonomic dysfunction, and life-threatening hypoventilation. Treatment requires immunotherapy (steroids, IVIG, plasmapheresis) and prompt surgical resection of the underlying teratoma.
